sections.html:
Westfield is a Hampden County city in the Pioneer Valley, about 10 miles west of Springfield and 95 miles west of Boston. It is large by land at 47.31 square miles, with 40,834 residents in the 2020 census, so it has plenty of open ground per person. A mayor and city council govern. The Westfield River splits the city into the North Side and the South Side, and the northwest corner is known as Wyben.

Neighbors include Southampton, Holyoke, West Springfield, Agawam, Southwick, Granville, Russell and Montgomery. Westfield State University anchors the south side, and Baystate Noble Hospital and Western Massachusetts Hospital are the main hospitals.

sections.h2: Why is Westfield called the Whip City?
sections.html:
The nickname comes from the buggy whip trade that made the city a manufacturing center in the 1800s. Settlers had farmed the river's rich soil for about 150 years, and the city later added bricks, cigars, bicycles, paper products, pipe organs, boilers, radiators and precision tools. Westfield was first settled in 1660, became a town in 1669 and became a city on November 2, 1920.

Manufacturing faded in the second half of the twentieth century, and the north side turned to warehousing. Housing today runs from older neighborhoods near the center to newer streets near the highways, so describe your house by its age and updates.

Westfield sits in a floodplain zone and is considered flood-prone. The Westfield River drops out of the Berkshire Hills through a large, steep, rocky watershed, which gives it a history of severe floods in the adjoining neighborhoods. Pumps, dikes, waterways and upstream dams help, but they do not remove the risk.

Winters are cold. At Westfield-Barnes Regional Airport the January mean high is about 33 degrees and the mean low about 13, and the record low is 20 below zero. Annual precipitation averages 48.39 inches.

  • Ask your insurer whether your address is in a mapped flood zone.
  • Keep records of any basement water, sump repairs or storm claims.
  • Service the heating system before showings, since buyers test it in winter.

If your house has a private well, ask the local health office about testing before you list.

The Massachusetts Turnpike (I-90) crosses just north of Westfield Center and meets I-91 about three miles east. U.S. 20 is the main east-west street, and U.S. 202 and Route 10 run north and south. The Great River Bridge over the Westfield River, called the Green Bridge, was doubled in the 2000s so each span carries one direction.

Pioneer Valley Transit Authority routes R10 and B23 connect to Springfield, West Springfield and Holyoke. Passenger trains no longer stop in the city. The nearest Amtrak and CTrail Hartford Line service is in Springfield, 9.6 miles east, and Bradley International Airport in Windsor Locks is 18 miles south. Westfield-Barnes Regional Airport offers charter service.

Westfield has generous green space for a city its size, and a buyer will notice it: Stanley Park, Amelia Park Ice Rink and Memorial Garden, the Columbia Greenway Rail Trail, East Mountain and the 114-mile Metacomet-Monadnock Trail, which crosses the city. The Westfield Athenaeum has been a free public library since 1868.

Westfield Public Schools run one preschool, five elementary schools, an intermediate school, a middle school and two high schools, Westfield High School and Westfield Technical Academy. Westfield River Elementary School opened on January 6, 2025, replacing Franklin Avenue and Abner Gibbs.

Westfield follows the same state procedure as every Massachusetts city. An abatement lowers a bill when the assessed value exceeds fair cash value, when an exemption applies, or when the classification is wrong. The burden of proof sits with the taxpayer, and the strongest evidence is recent sales of similar nearby houses.

  • File the abatement application with the assessors by the first installment due date.
  • The assessors have three months to decide.
  • The Appellate Tax Board hears appeals filed within three months of the decision.
  • Most single-family appeals use the informal procedure, which has no formal discovery.

Westfield's assessor posts local forms and deadlines. Call that office for the current ones.

sections.h2: Closing costs for a Westfield seller
sections.html:

Deed recording fee$155Hampden County Registry of Deeds
Deed excise tax$4.56 per $1,000 of taxable valueHampden County Registry of Deeds
Municipal lien certificate$80Hampden County Registry of Deeds

Westfield deeds are recorded at the Hampden County Registry of Deeds, which accepts cash and checks only. Your lender payoff, title work and any agent fee come on top, so ask the closing attorney for an itemized estimate before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: Selling a Westfield house fast: your options
sections.html:
Westfield owners usually weigh three paths. A listing can bring the strongest price when the house shows well. A private sale saves the commission but needs paperwork help. A cash sale closes quickly and skips the repair list.

For an inherited house, a flood-damaged basement or a home with tenants, speed and certainty often matter more than squeezing out the last dollar. Compare written offers, keep the closing date flexible, and ask each buyer how they handle title questions or an unpaid tax bill that has to be cleared at closing.

faqs.q: How many people live in Westfield, MA?
Is Westfield, MA in a floodplain?
faqs.a: Parts of the city lie in the Westfield River floodplain, and the city is considered flood-prone despite dikes and dams. Confirm your own address on the FEMA flood map and with your insurer.

faqs.q: What is the deed excise tax for a Westfield sale?
faqs.a: The Hampden County Registry of Deeds charges $4.56 per $1,000 of taxable value or fraction of $1,000, with no tax when the stated price is under $100.
Westfield State University anchors the south side of the city.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Westfield house that has water damage?
faqs.a: Yes. You can list it with disclosures, sell it to an investor or take a cash offer from a company that buys as is. Describe the damage honestly in writing so nothing surprises the buyer at closing.
